Arachnodactyly, joint laxity and spondylolisthesis define a skeletal and joint disorder.

Posterior displacement of the ocular lens defines the disease.
Disorder of hydroxyproline metabolism, generally benign; historical intellectual disability and hematuria reports do not establish common direct damage.

Pituitary hormone deficiency defines this subtype; visual impairment and neurological abnormalities occur below 30%; headache alone is insufficient.

Tumour arises at the hepatopancreatic ampulla, spanning the duodenal and terminal extrahepatic biliary interface; both anatomical parentages are supplied.
Obstruction of the gallbladder; the gallbladder is included in the hepatic axis.
Classic STAR deficiency impairs adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis; electrolyte disturbances remain within the metabolic_endocrine axis.
Persistent postpartum hyperprolactinemia causes galactorrhea and amenorrhea; the endocrine abnormality supplies an axis despite the obstetric setting.
Familial Alzheimer neurodegeneration with cerebral amyloid and prion pathology; coexisting prion pathology alone does not establish an infectious disease.
Primary tumour of the breast, an organ outside the axes; vascular differentiation alone does not establish cardiovascular organ dysfunction.
Central movement disorder defined by myoclonus and dystonia; muscle contractions do not establish muscle damage, and psychiatric features have no axis.
Plasma-cell neoplasm; approximately 80% arise in upper respiratory sites, supporting pulmonary as a common origin. Other anatomical sites are minorities.
The concept itself is a conjunctival disorder; ocular localization supports primary even though hyperemia alone would not justify secondary involvement.
Inherited calcium-sensing disorder with hypercalcemia and hypocalciuria; altered renal handling is not renal damage. Stones and ulcers occur below 30%.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 10/10 patients; no additional organ disease is established.
Congenital pituitary hormone deficiency with central antidiuretic hormone deficiency; no independent neurological or renal damage is established.
